accepted_answers.name: email-validator
accepted_answers.why: Validates deliverability-relevant syntax (including internationalised addresses) instead of an inevitably wrong regex.

accepted_answers.name: validators (URL) + urllib.parse
accepted_answers.why: Accepted for URLs: validators.url for one-liner checks, urllib.parse for structured parsing of components.

notes: Very strong consensus: the canonical email regex thread concludes a correct general regex is impractical; use a dedicated validator. Hand-rolled patterns reject valid addresses and accept invalid ones.
problem: Validating email addresses or URLs in Python with a hand-written regular expression.
